purpose: Test progressive intent formalization, branching representations and risk-proportional commitment gates.

activities.label: apply intent revisions and compile phase-specific representation policies
check commitment order and reversible action contract with independent oracle

queries.expression: can an emergent intent receive reversible alternative representations without being blocked
does execution remain unavailable until intent maturity, outcome verifiability and action contract are sufficient
are unselected representation plans retained as alternatives instead of being labeled wrong

assumptions: Intent revisions are declarative synthetic examples and do not represent a real participant.
JSON Patch supplies revision and branching mechanics without requiring a runtime dependency.
A reversible representation may be shown while task binding remains unknown.
Action contracts govern commitment and execution, not every act of exploration.
kill_tests: Premature commitment must block the progression.
A representation space without alternatives must block exploratory validity.
Invalid JSON Patch paths must not be silently ignored.
An action without independent verification must block final construction.
No human data, camera, network or generated-code execution is allowed.
unknowns: Whether progressive formalization improves human exploration or learning.
Whether retaining alternatives prevents premature convergence in real creative work.
How many branches a person can compare before the representation itself becomes overwhelming.
Whether a real application can expose enough state for a reversible effect contract.
Whether RFC 6902 patches remain sufficient for collaborative or long-lived intent histories.
